title: Back to top button
when: The user wants a floating button that takes the reader back to the top of a long page.
inputs: other fixed elements in the corners
prompt:
Goal: A small floating link that appears after scrolling, jumps to the top and moves focus there too.
Steps:
1. <a href="#top" class="to-top"> with visually hidden text Back to top and an arrow SVG with aria-hidden="true"; the header gets id="top" and tabindex="-1".
2. Show it once the header leaves view: an IntersectionObserver on the header toggles data-show.
3. Hide with visibility: hidden plus opacity so it leaves the Tab order while hidden.
4. Smooth scroll only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { html { scroll-behavior: smooth; } }.
5. Fixed at the bottom end with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), 48 px square, clear of chat widgets and sticky bars.
Quality bar:
- It works without JavaScript as a plain anchor.
- After the jump, keyboard focus starts at the top.
- It never covers form buttons.
Pitfalls:
- A scroll listener doing work on every pixel.
- An icon only control with no name.
- Forced smooth scrolling for reduced motion users.
Verify:
- [ ] The link has an accessible name.
- [ ] The SVG is aria-hidden.
- [ ] Hidden and unfocusable near the top.
- [ ] Reduced motion jumps instantly.
Output: The link before the closing body tag, its CSS and to-top.js.

examples.input: botao voltar ao topo no blog
examples.output: fixed arrow link to #top shown after the header scrolls away, smooth only without reduced motion
